page: Amazon Web Services r8id.16xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-hypervisor virtual instance equipped with 64 vCPUs derived from 32 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 480 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance supplies 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory rated at 7 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio, and integrates 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results show top-tier computational throughput in multi-core metrics, scoring 20,973 on Geekbench multi-core and registering top 10 percent placement for Clang software compilation and image processing. Memory throughput delivers 5,121.18 GB/sec in cached small-block reads and 191.69 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations. The instance also handles high I/O throughput, executing 112.39 million Redis SET operations per second and maintaining a static web serving throughput of 108.46 GB/sec.

In qualitative terms, the r8id.16xlarge offers high operational efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise tasks by bundling high-density DDR5 RAM with fast local NVMe storage on a single host. However, the lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy machine learning training, although its AMX extensions provide competitive CPU-based LLM inference. The instance is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput web serving, and memory-bound data analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8id.16xlarge is a high-capacity memory-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor at 3.9 GHz. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates 480 MB of L3 cache and supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. It delivers 512.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, 3,800 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage, and 30 Gbps baseline network throughput. Performance testing shows top-tier multi-threaded execution, exceeding 20,900 points in Geekbench multi-core, 112.39 million Redis operations per second, and 108.46 GB/sec in web serving throughput. Cost efficiency is driven by the co-location of large RAM reserves and direct-attached NVMe storage, making the instance optimal for enterprise in-memory caches, distributed databases, large-scale Clang builds, and CPU-driven inference pipelines without requiring GPU hardware.
